text:
Devon: Heads up — seeing repeated NVLink saturation on shared-pool-usw2-3 during tenant bursts, causing 95p token latency to spike ~180ms across gen workloads. Repro window: 2026-03-19 22:03 UTC. :warning:
Alex: Noted. Is it correlated to any specific tenant ID or tenant egress?
Devon: Yes — tenant t-alpha and t-zeta show simultaneous high KV cache miss + PCIe DMA bursts. NVLink counters show link utilization >92%.
Maria: Any new deployments? Could be a recent mass warmup.
Devon: No code deploys. Telemetry shows an increase in concurrent small requests (seq len <64) from those tenants.
Sanjay: If it's NVLink, routing to another rack won't help. We should consider isolating those tenants to a dedicated slice with reserved NVLink capacity.
Alex: Agree. Dedicated slices cost more though — do we have a quick eval on monthly uplift vs noise mitigation?
Maria: Rough calc: dedicated slice per 8xA100 equivalent is ~$12k/month (rough infra cost); need to compare to churn/credits. I'll pull historical incident cost.
Tess: Could we do interim shaping? e.g., egress shaping + kvcache aggressive TTL to reduce NVLink pressure.
Devon: I ran a quick patch on dev cluster: set tenant label `egress_heavy=true` and applied egress policer -> saw NVLink drop to ~60% and 95p latency back down.
Devon: Patch to mark tenant:
```
# mark tenant for egress shaping
curl -X POST https://internal-api/tenants/t-alpha/labels -d '{"labels": {"egress_heavy": "true"}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
Alex: Nice. Can we automate detection? e.g., an anomaly on NVLink util + kvcache miss rate => auto carveout or throttle?
Sanjay: We already have noise-detector that flags PCIe/NVLink anomalies but it doesn't tie to tenant labels. We can add a rule: if NVLink>80% and tenant_kv_miss_rate>0.6 for 2min, then tag and run soft-shape.
Tess: Soft-shape should be reversible and low-impact. Maybe reduce burst tokens to 50% for 30s and ramp.
Maria: For long term: propose 'egress-priority' routing — prefer dedicated pools for tenants with sustained egress. Also evaluate dedicated pool sizing to ensure NVLink headroom.
Devon: Ops playbook (sketch):
1) Detect: nvlink_util > 80% && kv_miss_rate > 0.6 for 2m => create alert
2) Auto-tag: attach label `egress_heavy=true` to offending tenant
3) Soft-shape: apply egress policer (50% burst cap) + aggressive kvcache TTL for 30s
4) If sustained > 10m => schedule dedicated carveout + prewarm (notify CS/Finance)
5) Fallback: if soft-shape fails, route to fallback model variant w/ lower memory/kvcost

Devon: Quick test results on dev: soft-shape cut NVLink util and tail almost immediately, no client errors observed.
oncall-sre-bot: Incident created INC-20260319-42, paging rotation notified.
Alex: I'll take cost model, will ping finance for rates. :+1:
Sanjay: I'll prototype tag rule this afternoon and put PR for review.
Tess: I'll schedule canary rollout to dev cluster after Sanjay's rule lands.
Maria: I'll draft a short email to CS with mitigations and ask for customer opt-in for dedicated slice trials.
Devon: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in #eng-infra in ~2 hours for status. :eyes:
